morning.caption:
COP31's first draft deal asks countries to scale carbon capture to at least 500 million tonnes a year by 2035. The world runs about 68 million today. The EU and a bloc including Saudi Arabia and India want changes before talks close Nov 20.

What it means for investors, regulators and industry at carbonenergynexus.com

midday.caption:
North Carolina regulators approved Duke Energy's first tariff for data centers of 50 MW or more: 10 to 15 year contracts, payment on at least 75% of contracted load and upfront grid costs. Data centers are 92% of Duke's new contracted demand.

More at carbonenergynexus.com

#DataCenters #PowerGrid #Utilities #EnergyMarkets

evening.caption:
ACME Group took a final investment decision on a $3.6 billion green ammonia plant in Odisha, India, sized for 760,000 tonnes a year by 2029. About 60% is sold to Indian fertilizer makers and Japan's IHI.

More at carbonenergynexus.com
